- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.1) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.1), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid immediate overshoot.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if 30d forecast is > 75 and true outcome is < 70, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next period.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +1.1, -1.1, +1.1), model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast to 3–5 day moving average of history.
